summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with altered mental status, hypotension, and a history of recurrent UTIs. She was found to have a multidrug-resistant Klebsiella UTI, confirmed by urine culture, and was treated with intravenous antibiotics, initially meropenem and later transitioned to ertapenem. Her delirium resolved within a day of admission, and hypotension improved with IV fluids. A PICC line was placed to complete a 7-day course of outpatient antibiotics. She remained stable with no complications, and her chronic conditions were managed without change. She was discharged home with nursing support for IV therapy and instructions to monitor for recurrent symptoms.
